instruction: Change the height of the picture to 18cm on slide 4 and set the font size of all textboxes to 28pt on slide 6.

command: import pyautogui; import time; pyautogui.hotkey('ctrl', 's'); time.sleep(0.5);

metadata.trajectory_summary: Agent successfully navigated to slide 3, selected the picture, changed its height to 20cm via Position and Size panel. Then navigated to slide 6 and changed all textbox font sizes to 40pt. Completed in 35 turns.
metadata.capability_extraction: Can navigate between slides in Impress, select shapes, modify dimensions via Position and Size panel, select all text in textboxes and change font size
metadata.task_rationale: Targets a different slide for picture resize (slide 4 instead of 3) and a different font size (28pt instead of 40pt) on the same slide 6, adding variety while testing same capabilities
metadata.explanation: Getter extracts picture height on slide 4 (first PICTURE shape) and font sizes of all textboxes on slide 6. Metric gives 0.5 partial credit for correct picture height (within 0.5cm tolerance) and 0.5 for all font sizes matching 28pt.

scoring_breakdown.picture_height: 0.5 - Picture height on slide 4 matches 18cm within tolerance
scoring_breakdown.font_sizes: 0.5 - All textbox font sizes on slide 6 match 28pt

llm_judge_reasons: Getter correctly uses 0-based slide indices: pic_slide_index=3 (slide 4) and font_slide_index=5 (slide 6), matching the instruction.
EMU-to-cm conversion (shape.height / 360000) and EMU-to-pt conversion (run.font.size / 12700) are both correct.
Metric correctly accesses expected parameters directly (expected.get('expected_height_cm')) since expected IS the rules dict for type='rule'.
Both instruction requirements are verified: picture height (0.5 credit) and font sizes (0.5 credit with proportional scoring).
Postconfig properly saves the file with Ctrl+S before evaluation, ensuring the getter reads the latest state.
Tolerances are reasonable: 0.5cm for picture height, 1.0pt for font size.
Minor note: getter only checks first PICTURE shape on slide 4, but instruction says 'the picture' (singular), which is appropriate.
